# Prompting Veo

Models: Veo 3.1, Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Lite. A good prompt runs about 1500 characters.

Name each reference where the prompt uses it as `@{ref:<ref>}`, with the exact ref you pass; Sceneform swaps in the model's own token, so wherever this guide names a token (`@Image1`, `Figure 1`), write the mention instead.

Veo takes one paragraph written in Google's own five-part order. Follow it, dropping any part the request does not need:

Cinematography, then subject, then action, then context, then style and ambiance.

Cinematography comes first because it carries the tone: shot size, camera position, any move, and the lens feel. Subject, action, and context are the three you always fill. Style and ambiance close the paragraph.

**Camera.** Use Google's documented vocabulary and invent nothing beyond it. Movement: dolly, tracking shot, crane shot, aerial view, slow pan, point of view, truck, pedestal, tilt, zoom, handheld, whip pan, arc, static. Composition: wide shot, close-up, extreme close-up, medium shot, full shot, establishing shot, over the shoulder, low angle, high angle, bird's-eye, worm's-eye, Dutch angle, two-shot. Lens: shallow depth of field, deep focus, soft focus, macro lens, wide-angle lens, telephoto, rack focus, lens flare, fisheye, dolly zoom. Unusual angles outside that list are not reliably supported.

**Speech.** Write it inline as an attribution and quoted words, with the delivery inside the attribution: a weary dock worker says, in a low voice, "We have to leave now." Keep spoken lines short enough for the chosen duration.

**Other sound.** Give it its own sentences with a label, never folded into the visual sentence:

SFX: thunder cracks somewhere behind the treeline.
Ambient noise: the low hum of a half-empty diner.

**Exclusions.** Veo responds badly to instructions phrased as prohibitions. Do not write "no cars" or "don't show a crowd". Describe the absence as part of the scene instead: "a deserted street with no traffic and no parked cars" reads as description, "no man-made structures" reads as an order and works less well.

**With reference images.** Open with a naming sentence that says what each reference is for, then the shot itself: "Using the provided images for the barista and the cafe interior, a medium shot of ..." Keep that opening identical if the request implies several shots of the same scene. Veo 3.1 and Veo 3.1 Fast take up to three reference images, of a single person, character, or product; Veo 3.1 Lite takes none, only a start and an end frame.

**With a start frame.** Describe the motion, the camera behaviour, any shift in light, and the sound. With both a start and an end frame, describe the single camera move that connects them rather than two separate scenes.

**Several beats in one clip.** Only when the request carries them, use bracketed timestamp ranges and repeat the subject's identifying details in each one, because Veo does not carry them forward:

[00:00-00:02] Medium shot from behind a young mechanic in a grease-marked jacket, walking into the bay.
[00:02-00:05] The same mechanic, still in the grease-marked jacket, turns toward the camera. SFX: a socket wrench clatters onto concrete.

**Avoid.** Asking for more than one video in a single prompt: it degrades the result. Stacking mood words where a concrete description of scale, atmosphere and colour would do the work. Writing in a language other than English, which Google has not evaluated.
